attractions.name: Ratti Gali Lake
attractions.description: A stunning high-altitude alpine lake reached by jeep and a hiking trail, one of AJK's most photographed natural spots.

attractions.name: Kel & Sharda Villages
attractions.description: Scenic mountain villages along the Neelum River, gateways to further trekking routes and alpine meadows.

attractions.name: Sharda Peeth (ancient ruins)
attractions.description: Ruins of an ancient Hindu/Buddhist center of learning, historically significant to Kashmiri heritage.

food_places.name: Neelum Valley riverside dhabas
food_places.specialty: Fresh trout fish and traditional Kashmiri dishes

transportation.route: Local/intercity coach via AJK highway network
transportation.notes: Most common route to AJK's capital
Daily coach services connect to the twin cities
Shared vans and jeeps are common for mountain roads

weather_info.climate_type: Mountain climate with mild summers and cold, snowy winters at higher elevations
weather_info.avoid_months: December to February (heavy snow, road closures in upper valleys)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild and green, 20-30°C, the main tourist season
Cold, often below freezing at higher elevations; upper valleys get heavy snowfall
Heavy rain in places, landslide risk on mountain roads

travel_tips.tip: Visit Neelum Valley between April and August for the best weather and open mountain roads.
Jeeps are often needed for higher valleys; book local transport in advance during peak season.
Check current travel advisories before visiting, as with any AJK district near the Line of Control.

history.founded: A historic valley along the Neelum River, long inhabited by Kashmiri and Gujjar mountain communities
history.city_history: Neelum Valley, headquartered at Athmuqam, runs along the Line of Control and is considered one of the most scenic valleys in Azad Kashmir, though parts were affected by the 2005 earthquake and subsequent conflict-related disruptions to tourism.
history.province_history: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) is a self-governing territory administered by Pakistan since 1947, following the First Kashmir War. It retains its own president, prime minister, and legislative assembly, while Pakistan handles defense and foreign affairs. The region is known for its lush river valleys, forested mountains, and lakes fed by Himalayan glaciers.
